findings: The plan now states the positive-pair law, marginal negative law, one-negative iid triplets, bounded representation class, collision probability, average binary task distribution and uniform task labels used in the main theorem.

Theorem 4.1’s class-mean bound and its (1−tau) denominator are explicit; Theorem 4.5 now defines the collision-conditioned class law nu, covariance, within-class term s(f), and beta/eta factors. The empirical contrastive minimizer is an existence premise; an approximate selector needs an extra additive optimization term.

The optional margin corollary remains subordinate to the exact classwise sub-Gaussian and mean-margin assumptions. It is not a theorem about general multiclass top-1 performance or SimCLR/augmentation semantics.

findings: The ELBO consumer now states positive finite evidence normalizer, proper posterior, q absolutely continuous with respect to the posterior, and finite absolute log-integrability, exactly matching BCS-22’s generic decomposition contract.

The pathwise gradient result is a separate local theorem: parameter-independent base noise, pointwise C1 integrand, and an integrable derivative envelope on compact parameter neighborhoods justify differentiation by the existing dominated-convergence theorem.

Kingma–Welling motivate pathwise differentiation under “mild” conditions but do not state a complete dominated-differentiation theorem; the scaffold appropriately assigns that proof locally and makes no posterior recovery/identifiability claim.

findings: Hyvärinen’s score identity is restricted to Lebesgue densities on R^n, differentiable data density, differentiable model score, finite second moments of data/model scores, integrable divergence term, and the vanishing product boundary condition p_data(x) psi_theta(x)→0.

The partition function is required finite and positive for normalized likelihoods, while differentiation in x removes its constant. CD-k compares the exact data-minus-equilibrium model gradient with a finite reconstruction chain and omits the derivative of the chain distribution.

Hyvärinen states a parametric consistency result under correct specification/identifiability and a global minimizer, but the paper’s sample argument invokes pointwise LLN; without uniform convergence/argmin conditions it is not promoted to a general consistency theorem.

The paper’s pointwise statement p_data(x) psi_theta(x)->0 at infinity is not by itself a multivariate integrated boundary-flux proof. The plan strengthens the local theorem to compactly supported cutoff integration by parts; finite score L2 gives p psi in L1 and a cutoff derivative O(1/R) makes the boundary error vanish. The local cutoff/limit proof remains an item-author obligation.

findings: The ideal discriminator theorem is stated only for data and generator densities with respect to a common dominating measure and an unrestricted measurable discriminator; the pointwise formula is defined only almost everywhere on the union of supports.

Substituting the discriminator yields C(G)=−log 4+2 JS(p_data||p_G), with equality iff the distributions agree. The source’s distribution-space convergence proposition assumes enough capacity, optimal discriminator at every generator step and sufficiently small distribution updates.
No conclusion is transferred to finite neural parameterizations or alternating gradient training; source experiments/mode-collapse discussion are not theorems.
